# References

Chib, S., & Greenberg, E. (1995). Understanding the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm. *The American Statistician*, 49(4), 327-335.

Rizzo, M. L. (2019). *Statistical Computing with R* (2nd ed.). CRC Press.

Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks. Provincial (Stream) Water Quality Monitoring Network (PWQMN) 2025 data. 

<!-- Add further references above. Also include a detailed summary of how generative AI was used in this project. -->

**Use of generative AI:** Claude (Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5) was used on November 21, 2026 to clean the environmental dataset. All AI-generated code and output were reviewed by the authors, who remain responsible for the content of this report.

- *Data cleaning.* Claude wrote R code to import the PWQMN 2025 CSV and extract the total phosphorus records. The code reads the file with Latin-1 encoding, removes 74 duplicated rows (identical site, date, time, laboratory sample ID and result), and replaces the 20 below-detection-limit results (recorded as `<0.2`) with half the detection limit. Samples carrying laboratory remark codes are flagged but kept. This left 3,690 samples from 449 sites.

- *Generalising the sampler's proposal distribution.* On November 22, 2026, the authors used Claude in a chat to review our original `mh_sampler()` against Rizzo (2019, Ch. 11) and Chib and Greenberg (1995). The review found that the sampler hard-coded a symmetric normal random-walk proposal and had no Hastings correction term, so it could not support our planned comparison of proposal distributions. Based on this review, the authors wrote their own prompt for an AI coding agent (Claude Opus 5.5) working in our package repository, instructing it to change the sampler so that it adheres more closely to the simulation study described in our project proposal, in particular the comparison of different proposal distributions. The agent:
  - changed `mh_sampler()` to take the proposal as an argument and to use the full Metropolis-Hastings acceptance ratio, including the Hastings correction (Rizzo, 2019, eq. 11.3), first evaluated on the log scale and later changed to the raw density scale, as in Rizzo (2019), with a `testthat` test confirming that the raw-scale sampler reproduces the earlier log-scale chains;
  - created a new file, `R/proposals.R`, containing three proposal constructors: `normal_rw()` (symmetric normal random walk, reproducing the original sampler), `lognormal_rw()` (asymmetric multiplicative random walk for positive targets) and `gamma_independence()` (independence sampler), each with input checks;
  - made the sampler reject proposals whose target density is undefined, and updated the roxygen documentation, examples and `testthat` tests;
  - regenerated the help files (`man/`) and `NAMESPACE` with `devtools::document()`.

  The authors reviewed the generated code, and the choice of proposals, the acceptance rule and the overall design of the simulation study remain the authors' own.
